from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Transformation View", [
            "Linear transformations stretch and rotate the space.",
            "A vector 'v' maps to a new vector 'Av'.",
            "Typically, 'v' changes its direction after transformation."
        ])
        
        # Setup grid and vector
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.5}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(grid, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        v_start = np.array([1, 1, 0])
        v_obj = Arrow(ORIGIN, v_start, color="#FF00FF")
        v_label = Text("v", color="#FF00FF", font_size=20).next_to(v_obj.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        v_group = VGroup(v_obj, v_label)
        
        # Adjust position of the vector to be relative to the grid
        v_group.move_to(grid.c2p(0.5, 0.5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(grid), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(v_group), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Transformation
        matrix_a = [[1.5, 0.5], [0.5, 1.5]]
        
        # Apply matrix to vector
        v_end_2d = np.dot(matrix_a, v_start[:2])
        v_end = np.array([v_end_2d[0], v_end_2d[1], 0])
        v_av = Arrow(ORIGIN, v_end, color="#00FFFF")
        v_av_label = Text("Av", color="#00FFFF", font_size=20).next_to(v_av.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        v_av_group = VGroup(v_av, v_av_label)
        v_av_group.move_to(grid.c2p(v_end[0]/2, v_end[1]/2)) # Map v_end to the grid context
        
        self.play(
            grid.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_a),
            ReplacementTransform(v_group, v_av_group),
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.play(
            v_av_group.animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
            v_av_label.animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Visualize a 2D plane under a transformation.",
            "Most vectors change direction as the plane moves.",
            "Some special vectors stay on their original span."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Concept", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid and plane
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        plane_label = Text("Plane", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(plane_label, 'A1')
        self.add(plane)
        
        # Vector
        vec = Vector(direction=[1, 1, 0], color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(vec, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        vec_label = Text("v", font_size=24, color=PURPLE)
        self.add(vec_label)
        vec_label.next_to(vec.get_end(), UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(plane), Write(plane_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec), FadeIn(vec_label))
        self.play(Rotate(vec, angle=PI/3, about_point=plane.get_center()))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        special_vec = Vector(direction=[2, 0, 0], color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(special_vec, 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        special_label = Text("Lucky", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(special_label, 'E4')
        
        self.play(Create(special_vec), Write(special_label))
        self.play(Transform(special_vec, special_vec.copy().scale(1.5), run_time=2))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application Summary", [
            "Eigenvalues and vectors are used in stability analysis.",
            "They enable powerful tools like image compression.",
            "They are fundamental to modern quantum mechanics."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        network = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(10)])
        network.arrange_in_grid(2, 5, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(network, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        network_label = Text("Network", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(network_label, 'A3', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(network), Write(network_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        key_nodes = VGroup(*[network[i] for i in [0, 4, 7, 9]])
        self.play(key_nodes.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        rank_labels = VGroup(*[Text("Rank", color="#FFFF00", font_size=16) for _ in range(4)])
        for i, node in enumerate(key_nodes):
            self.place_at_grid(rank_labels[i], 'F'+str(i+2), scale_factor=0.8)
            rank_labels[i].next_to(node, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(rank_labels))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometry of Linear Transformations: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
outline.target_audience: University students (Undergraduate level, introductory Linear Algebra)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Transformation View
sections.content: Briefly define a linear transformation as a stretching/rotating grid. Visualize a vector 'v' moving to 'Av'. Most vectors change direction during this transformation.
sections.example: Visualize a grid of square tiles being sheared and stretched by a matrix A.

sections.title: Defining Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues
sections.content: Introduce the 'staying put' concept: Eigenvectors are special vectors that do not change direction when the transformation is applied; they only scale by a factor λ (the eigenvalue). Formula: Av = λv.
sections.example: A spinning globe: The axis of rotation is the eigenvector (it doesn't move), and the eigenvalue represents the rotation speed/scale factor.

sections.title: Visualizing the Concept
sections.content: Use a graphical animation showing a 2D plane. Show a vector rotating, then highlight the 'lucky' vectors that remain on their original span line while stretching or shrinking.
sections.example: A vector pointing from the center of a clock to the number 3, which stays pointing at 3 even if the clock face is stretched horizontally.

sections.title: Constructing an Eigenbasis
sections.content: Explain that if we find enough linearly independent eigenvectors, they form a new coordinate system—an 'eigenbasis'. In this basis, the complex transformation matrix becomes a simple diagonal matrix.
sections.example: A character navigating a maze: Instead of using North/South coordinates (standard basis), they use the 'Eigen-directions' (the paths of least resistance), making the math of their movement trivial.

sections.title: Real-World Application Summary
sections.content: Briefly connect the theory to real-world impact: Stability analysis, image compression (PCA), and quantum mechanics.
sections.example: A search engine algorithm using eigenvectors to rank the importance of 'nodes' (webpages) in a giant network.
